cases.title: Call with no credentials; the spec marks this operation as open
cases.expect: 2xx is right only if it is meant to be public: confirm that with the user, and that nothing private is in the body

cases.title: Call with no credentials at all (no Authorization header, no cookie)
cases.expect: 401 or 403 with the declared error shape and no data; the spec says this needs bearerAuth

cases.title: Send text where a number or boolean is expected: limit=twelve
cases.expect: 400 or 422; never a 500 and never a silently coerced value

cases.title: Send -1 and then 0 in each numeric input: limit (query)
cases.expect: rejected when the schema sets a minimum above it, otherwise a sensible result; never a 500

cases.title: Call with no credentials at all (no Authorization header, no cookie)
cases.expect: 401 or 403 with the declared error shape and no data; the spec says this needs bearerAuth

cases.title: Send the body without each required field in turn: email, name
cases.expect: 400 or 422 naming the field; nothing created or changed

cases.title: Send each field with a value of the wrong type: email=12345, name=12345, role=12345, nickname=12345, age="twelve"
cases.expect: 400 or 422; the value must not be coerced silently (for example "12" stored as 12)

cases.title: Send null in each field that is not nullable: email, name, role, age
cases.expect: 400 or 422 for each one; never a 500

cases.title: Send a value outside the allowed set: role=not-a-valid-choice
cases.expect: 400 or 422 listing the allowed values

cases.title: Add a field the schema does not declare: "unexpected_field": "proof"
cases.expect: ignored, or 400 when the schema forbids extra fields; never stored or echoed back as if it were real

cases.title: Put a 100000-character string in each string field in turn: email, name, role, nickname
cases.expect: 413 or 400 within the usual response time; never a timeout, a 500 or an unbounded stored value

cases.title: Send text that looks like a query fragment, as plain data, in each string field: "Smith' OR 'a'='a"
cases.expect: stored and returned exactly as sent (it is only text), or rejected by a length or format rule; never a 500 and never a changed result set

cases.title: Send text that looks like markup, as plain data, in each string field: "Jo & "
cases.expect: returned exactly as sent, as JSON data; never a 500 (escaping on display is the web app's job)

cases.title: Send -1 and then 0 in each numeric input: age (body)
cases.expect: rejected when the schema sets a minimum above it, otherwise a sensible result; never a 500

cases.title: Call with no credentials at all (no Authorization header, no cookie)
cases.expect: 401 or 403 with the declared error shape and no data; the spec says this needs bearerAuth

cases.title: As test account B, use a value of id that belongs to account A
cases.expect: 403 or 404, and none of A's data in the body

cases.title: Use a value that matches no record: id=999999999
cases.expect: 404 with the declared error shape; never a 500

cases.title: Send text where a number or boolean is expected: id=twelve
cases.expect: 400 or 422; never a 500 and never a silently coerced value

cases.title: Send -1 and then 0 in each numeric input: id (path)
cases.expect: rejected when the schema sets a minimum above it, otherwise a sensible result; never a 500

cases.title: Property-based fuzz run over the whole spec, when a fuzzer such as Schemathesis is installed (check with /proof-doctor --for proof-api)
cases.expect: no 500s and no response that breaks its schema; save the run's output as evidence. Without a fuzzer: skip fuzz-run --note "no fuzzer installed"
